Here’s the full 12-week plan summary, integrating your upgraded training (including intensified Phase 2), cardio, glycaemic-control nutrition, and recovery guardrails. Start date: 2026-06-01. Primary goals: improve insulin sensitivity via progressive resistance training, reduce body fat at a steady pace, avoid under-fuelling/overtraining, and keep cycles as stable as possible.

Global structure
- Frequency: 3 resistance sessions/week (A, B, C)
- Cardio: Zone 2 base + post-meal walks; limited HIIT (see details)
- Session length: 50–65 minutes
- Intensity: RPE-based progression
- Steps: 7,000–10,000/day (gradually increase by +500/day every 1–2 weeks if recovery is good)
- Monitoring: weekly check-ins (energy, sleep, hunger/cravings, mood, cycle notes, top-set RPEs, weight trend)

Phase 1: Foundation and Technique (Weeks 1–3; 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-21)
Goal: establish technique, consistency, recoverability; build base aerobic work. RPE 6–7.

Week 1 (Jun 1–7)
- Lift A
  - Back squat or goblet squat 3x6 @ RPE 6
  - RDL 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - Half-kneeling Pallof press 3x10/side
  - Seated cable row 3x10
- Lift B
  - Bench press or DB bench 3x6 @ RPE 6
  - Split squat 3x8/side @ RPE 6
  - Lat pulldown 3x8–10
  - Hip thrust 3x8 @ RPE 6
- Lift C
  - Trap-bar or conventional deadlift 3x5 @ RPE 6
  - Overhead press 3x6 @ RPE 6
  - One-arm DB row 3x10/side
  - Face pull 3x12
- Cardio:
  - Post-meal walks: 10–15 min after lunch/dinner on 5 days
  - Zone 2: 1 x 20 min (RPE 4–5)

Week 2
- Keep exercises; add 1 set to first main lift if RPE ≤7 last week.
- Progress +1 rep or small load bump as tolerated.
- Add:
  - A: Band lateral walk 2x12/side
  - B: Incline DB curl 2x12
  - C: Triceps pressdown 2x12
- Cardio:
  - Post-meal walks most days
  - Zone 2: 2 x 20–25 min

Week 3
- Aim RPE 7 on last sets; maintain exercise menu.
- Optional finisher once: 6–8 min bike 20s hard/100s easy (cap RPE 8).
- Cardio:
  - Post-meal walks 15 min after 1–2 meals most days
  - Zone 2: 1 x 30 min + 1 x 20–25 min

Phase 2: Progressive Strength and Hypertrophy — Intensified (Weeks 4–7; 2026-06-22 to 2026-07-19)
Goal: push intensity safely; build lean mass and strength. Key format: top set @ RPE ~8 + back-off volume. Cardio steady, HIIT minimal.

Safety guardrails (every week): if sleep <6.5 h or two negative recovery markers, cap RPE at 7–7.5 and remove HIIT/finishers that week. Add 25–50 g carbs on training days in this phase.

Week 4
- A (Lower)
  - Back squat: top set 1x5 @ RPE 8; back-offs 3x5 @ -8–10%
  - RDL 4x6 @ RPE 7.5
  - Walking lunge 3x10/leg
  - Seated row 3x8–10
  - Copenhagen plank 2x30s/side
- B (Upper)
  - Bench: top set 1x5 @ RPE 8; back-offs 3x5 @ -8–10%
  - Assisted pull-up 4x5–6 @ RPE 7.5–8
  - Incline DB press 3x8–10
  - Single-arm cable row 3x10/side
  - Lateral raise 3x12
- C (Hinge/Posterior)
  - Trap-bar deadlift: top set 1x4 @ RPE 8; back-offs 3x4 @ -8–10%
  - Hip thrust 4x6–8 @ RPE 7.5–8 (2–3 s hold)
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x8/leg
  - Face pull 3x12; Pallof press 3x10/side
- Cardio: Zone 2, 2 x 30–35 min; post-meal walks most days.

Week 5 (clusters/pauses)
- A: Squat clusters 3x(2+2) @ RPE 8; RDL 4x5; Leg press 2x10–12; Seated row 3x8–10; Farmer’s carry 2x40–60 m
- B: Bench paused 4x4 @ RPE 7.5–8; Pull-up 4x4–6; DB incline 3x8; Cable row 3x10; Push-up AMRAP leaving 2 RIR
- C: Deadlift clusters 3x(1+1+1) @ RPE 8; Hip thrust 4x5–6; Split squat 3x8/leg; Ham curl 2x10–12; Face pull 2x12–15
- Cardio: Zone 2, 2 x 30–35 min; 1 HIIT optional (bike 8–10 x 40s hard/2:00 easy) if recovery is green.

Week 6 (heavier top sets, trimmed back-off)
- A: Squat heavy triple @ RPE 8; back-off 2x3 @ -8–10%; RDL 3x5; Lunge 2x10/leg; Seated row 3x8–10
- B: Bench heavy triple @ RPE 8; back-off 2x3; Pull-up 4x4–5; Incline DB 3x6–8; Lateral raise 2x12–15
- C: Deadlift heavy double @ RPE 8; back-off 2x2; Hip thrust 3x5–6; Bulgarian SS 2x8/leg; Face pull 2x12–15
- Cardio: Zone 2, 2 x 30–35 min; up to 1 HIIT (same template) if green; keep post-meal walks.

Week 7 (micro-peak with singles @8)
- A: Squat single @ RPE 8; back-off 3x3 @ -10%; RDL 3x4–5; Leg press 2x10; Copenhagen plank 2x30–40 s
- B: Bench single @ RPE 8; back-off 3x3; Pull-up 4x3–5; DB incline 2x8; Cable row 2x10
- C: Deadlift single @ RPE 8; back-off 3x2; Hip thrust 3x4–5; Split squat 2x8/leg; Farmer’s carry 2x40–60 m
- Cardio: Zone 2 only 2 x 30 min; no HIIT this week. Keep walks.

Phase 3: Intensification and Metabolic Support (Weeks 8–10; 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-09)
Goal: consolidate strength, keep accessories modest, add controlled density without spiking stress. RPE 7.5–8 on priority lifts.

Week 8
- A: Squat 4x3 @ RPE 7.5–8; RDL 3x5; Lunge 3x8/leg; Chest-supported row 3x8–10; Side plank 2x30–45 s
- B: Bench 4x3 @ RPE 7.5–8; Assisted pull-up 4x3–5; DB incline 3x8; Cable row 3x10; Rear delt fly 2x12–15
- C: Trap-bar deadlift 4x3 @ RPE 7.5–8; Hip thrust 3x5–6; Split squat 3x8/leg; Face pull 3x12; Pallof press 3x10/side
- Density: 1 light EMOM this week (8 min: 5 KB swings + 5 bodyweight squats), not on deadlift day.
- Cardio: Zone 2, 2 x 30–35 min; 1 HIIT optional if fully green.

Week 9
- Squat and Bench: 3x(2+2) clusters @ RPE ~8; other lifts as Week 8.
- Cardio: Zone 2, 2 x 30 min; 1 HIIT optional (8–10 x 45–60 s @ RPE 7–7.5 / 2:00 easy) if recovery is green.

Week 10 (submax peak for e1RM)
- Squat: work to heavy triple @ RPE 8, then 2x3 @ -7.5–10%
- Deadlift: heavy double @ RPE 8, then 2x2 @ -7.5–10%
- Bench: heavy triple @ RPE 8, then 2x3 back-off
- Accessories minimal: 2 movements/session only
- Cardio: 1–2 x 25–30 min Zone 2; no HIIT

Short answer: no to daily HIIT. With PCOS, insulin resistance, and the known risk of under-fuelling/overtraining, daily HIIT is far more likely to backfire (sleep disruption, elevated cortisol, appetite dysregulation, stalled strength, longer cycles) than to accelerate results. The strongest, most consistent data for PCOS favor regular resistance training plus low-to-moderate aerobic work, with HIIT used sparingly.

What the evidence and experience suggest
- HIIT can improve insulin sensitivity and VO2max, but benefits plateau quickly and the stress cost is high. In PCOS cohorts, 1–3 HIIT sessions/week show benefit; more isn’t better.
- Resistance training is first-line for insulin sensitivity (as your endo advised). It needs to be fueled and recovered from to work.
- High-frequency HIIT commonly elevates perceived stress, worsens sleep, and degrades lifting performance—exactly what we want to avoid.

A smart compromise: “HIIT-lite” caps with clear rules
- Cap HIIT at 1–2 sessions/week during higher-intensity lifting phases (like your Phase 2); at most 2 sessions/week in lighter weeks. Never on consecutive days; never the day before heavy deadlifts.
- Keep intervals submaximal (RPE 7–8, not all-out). Total hard time 6–10 minutes/session.
- Prefer low-impact modalities (bike, rower, sled). Running sprints add orthopedic stress.

Recommended HIIT templates (pick one per week to start)
- Bike RPE 7–8 “on/off”:
  - Warm-up 8–10 min easy with 2 short pickups.
  - 8–10 rounds: 40 s hard (RPE 7–8) / 2:00 easy.
  - Cool down 5–8 min.
- Rower power intervals:
  - Warm-up 8 min.
  - 10 x 30 s hard strokes (RPE 7.5–8) / 90 s easy.
  - Cool down 5–8 min.
- Sled push repeats (great for glucose, low eccentric load):
  - Warm-up walk + 2 easy pushes.
  - 8–12 pushes of 15–25 m at strong pace; walk back for recovery (60–90 s).
- KB swing EMOM (technique-dependent):
  - 10 min EMOM: 12 swings in minute 1, 8–10 incline push-ups in minute 2, repeat (stop if form degrades).

- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): no HIIT. Build base and lifting tolerance.

- Weaker training stimulus → less muscle retention → lower resting metabolic rate over time.
- In PCOS, under-fuelling can exacerbate cycle irregularity and symptoms.

- Aim for 0.3–0.7% body weight loss per week (about 0.2–0.5 kg/week for many). That’s typically a 300–500 kcal/day average deficit.

- Carbs: 3–4 g/kg on lifting days; 2–3 g/kg on rest days. Keep most carbs earlier in the day and around training.

- Fiber: 25–40 g/day and hydrate well.

- Front-load: bigger breakfast/lunch, moderate dinner.

- Use 250–300 kcal “hunger anchors” at meals: 30–40 g protein + high-volume veg.

A true 1RM test at the end of Phase 3 isn’t ideal for this client right now. Phase 3 already peaks submaximally (RPE ~8) and is followed by a deload in Phase 4 to consolidate strength and manage total stress. A maximal test would add neural and systemic stress, increase injury risk, and can disrupt sleep/recovery—counterproductive for insulin sensitivity and for the fat-loss plan you’re running.

Better options that still give a clear strength benchmark
- Estimated 1RM (e1RM) from submax sets: Use a heavy triple or double at RPE 8 and calculate e1RM. This keeps 1–2 reps in reserve while giving valid comparisons over time.
- AMRAP at a fixed percentage: For example, 85% e1RM for max reps (stop 1 rep before form breaks). Track reps to gauge progress without maxing.
- Velocity-based estimate (if you have a bar speed device): Use a load–velocity profile to estimate 1RM at safer intensities.

Recommended test week (end of Week 10 or start of Week 11)
- Keep Phase 3 Week 10 as written (heavy triple/double @ RPE 8). Record top sets and use an RPE-based e1RM table or app.
- If you prefer a more formal test, do a “submax test” at the start of Week 11 before deload volume:
  - Squat: single @ RPE 8; back-off 2x3 @ -10%
  - Bench: single @ RPE 8; back-off 2x3 @ -10%
  - Deadlift: single @ RPE 8; back-off 2x2 @ -10%
  - Use those RPE 8 singles to compute e1RM. Then proceed with the lighter deload sets for skill and recovery.
- Guardrails: cut the day short if technique degrades, bar speed falls sharply, or RPE exceeds 8.5. No grinders.

How to calculate e1RM quickly (example)
- Take the heaviest clean set with RIR 1–2 (RPE 8–9).
- Use a standard RIR chart or calculator. Rough guide:
  - Triple @ RPE 8 ≈ 90–92% 1RM → e1RM = load / 0.91 (approx).
  - Double @ RPE 8 ≈ 92–94% 1RM → e1RM = load / 0.93 (approx).
  - Single @ RPE 8 ≈ 92–94% 1RM → e1RM = load / 0.93 (approx).
- Be consistent with the same method next block.

If you still want a true 1RM day
- Push it to the end of Phase 4 (Week 12) or the start of the next block after a full deload and a low-stress week.
- Do only one lift per day, with full warm-up and strict stop-rules:
  - Day 1: Squat to 1RM (no more than 3 attempts above 90%), then 2x2 @ 80% and done.
  - Day 3: Bench 1RM
  - Day 5: Deadlift 1RM
- Fuel like a meet day: high-carb meals the day prior and same-day pre-lift carbs; sleep ≥8 h night before.
- Cancel if sleep is poor, cycle symptoms flare, or fasting glucose runs high.

Why this approach fits PCOS and your program
- Keeps intensity high enough to show clear progress while minimizing stress load.
- Preserves quality training in Phase 3 and leverages Phase 4 deload for adaptation.
- Reduces risk of under-fuelling consequences and sleep disruption that can worsen insulin sensitivity.

Bottom line: Use RPE 8 singles/doubles or heavy triples to estimate 1RMs at the end of Phase 3, then consider a true 1RM after the deload if recovery, sleep, and glucose markers are green.

Cardio overview across 12 weeks
- Post-meal walks: 10–15 min after 1–2 meals on most days (keystone habit)
- Zone 2 minutes per week:
  - Weeks 1–3: build to 50–60 min → 60–80 min → 80–100 min
  - Weeks 4–7: maintain 60–70 min/week (two sessions of 30–35 min)
  - Weeks 8–10: 60–70 min/week; hold steady
  - Weeks 11–12: 50–90 min/week as recovery allows
- HIIT caps:
  - Weeks 1–3: none
  - Weeks 4–7: at most 1 session in Weeks 5–6; none in Week 7
  - Weeks 8–10: 1 session in Weeks 8–9 if recovery is green; none in Week 10
  - Weeks 11–12: optional 1 in Week 11; none in Week 12
- Modality: brisk walk, incline treadmill, bike, elliptical, rower, sled. Avoid back-to-back HIIT days and the day before heavy deadlifts.

Nutrition plan for glycaemic control and fat loss
- Calories: start near maintenance, then move to a modest 12–15% deficit. Weekly average loss target 0.3–0.7% BW. Run a “flex deficit”: nearer maintenance on lifting days, larger deficit on cardio/rest days.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day across 3–4 meals (25–40 g/meal)
- Carbs: 3–4 g/kg on lifting days; 2–3 g/kg on rest days; front-load earlier in the day and around training
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, favor mono-/polyunsaturated
- Fiber: 25–40 g/day; choose intact carbs (oats, barley, legumes, whole grains, potatoes with skin); berries/apples/pears preferred fruits
- Meal timing:
  - Pre: 25–40 g protein + 30–60 g low-GI carbs 60–120 min before training
  - Post: 25–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs within 1–2 h
  - Order meals: veg → protein/fat → starch; add 1–2 tsp vinegar/lemon to carb meals
  - Don’t train fasted; avoid very large high-fat/high-carb dinners
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + 500–1000 ml on training/heat days; electrolytes for long/hot sessions
- Supplements (coordinate with MD): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega-3 (1–2 g EPA/DHA if fish intake low); vitamin D if deficient; magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg if tolerated; inositol (myo ± D-chiro 40:1, ~2–4 g/day); iron only if deficient
- Dining out tips: protein-forward, extra veg, sauces on side; start with salad/veg

Weight-loss acceleration without crashing
- Run the bulk of the deficit on non-lifting days (−300 to −500 kcal), keep lifting days near maintenance (−0 to −200 kcal) to protect performance
- If plateau 2–3 weeks with good recovery: add 10–15 min to one Zone 2 session OR trim 100–150 kcal on 2–3 rest days; keep protein steady
- If hunger 8–10/10, sleep worsens, or lifts stall: add 25–50 g carbs/day, pause HIIT, hold loads for 1 week
- Optional refeed: +50–75 g carbs once weekly on a heavy lower day if stress/sleep falter
- Hard floor if client insists on “aggressive”: calories ≥22–24 kcal/kg/day; carbs ≥2 g/kg/day during intensified lifting; mandatory diet break (7 days at maintenance) after 3–4 weeks

Recovery and autoregulation
- Sleep: 7.5–9 h/night; consistent routine
- Stress: 5–10 min/day breathing or mindfulness; AM sunlight walks
- Readiness rules each training day:
  - Green: proceed as written
  - Yellow (one negative marker): cap RPE at 7.5; skip finishers/HIIT
  - Red (two+ negative markers): reduce main-lift volume by 1 set, cap RPE at 7, replace cardio with easy walks
- Menstrual/cycle adjustments: if period starts or PMS-like symptoms with low energy, swap that day’s session for Zone 2 or mobility; don’t “make up” missed volume later

Testing and progress tracking
- Use Week 10 heavy double/triple @ RPE 8 to compute e1RM for squat/bench/deadlift
- Optional RPE 8 singles at the start of Week 11 to refine e1RM, then deload volume
- Track weekly: body weight trend, waist, step count, top-set loads and RPEs, sleep duration, hunger (0–10), mood, and cycle notes
- Decide next block emphasis in Week 12: e.g., pull-ups, lower-body strength, or body recomposition
